name: Vercel

facts.value: Generally available Vercel-hosted Linux microVMs on Hobby, Pro and Enterprise
facts.notes: Requires a Vercel account and project; no deployed application is required. Hobby is restricted to non-commercial personal use and hard usage quotas. Pro has a $20/month platform fee with one deploying seat and shared $20/month usage credit; Enterprise pricing and quotas are custom. Drives are public beta; Secure Compute is a purchased Enterprise feature, not BYOC.

facts.value: Vercel's Sandbox comparison explicitly says self-hosting is not currently offered
facts.notes: Vercel's 2026-09-04 comparison explicitly says Sandbox does not currently offer BYOC/self-hosting infrastructure flexibility. The open SDK/CLI and image sources are client/developer artifacts, not a service installation contract. This is a scoped product-specific negative; no separate hosted-service deployment claim.

The Sandbox comparison says BYOC is not currently offered, but broader Enterprise AWS BYOC/platform material does not establish Sandbox inclusion or the control-plane/execution model. Secure Compute is Vercel-run peering, not customer-account execution. Preserve the product-scope conflict as unknown; /docs/byoc returned 404 in the source review. See audit E04.

facts.value: JavaScript/TypeScript and Python
facts.notes: Official packages are @vercel/sandbox (JS/TS) and vercel.sandbox (Python); CLI is separate. No official Go Sandbox SDK was documented in reviewed official sources as of 2026-10-08. This is a bounded comparison inference, not vendor denial; guest Go and generic HTTP clients are distinct. See audit E02.

Official docs list JS/TS and Python SDKs, CLI, and integrations; they do not exhaust third-party projects. Keep community SDK inventory unknown rather than infer absence from official sources. No vendor support or endorsement of external clients implied. See final audit correction.

facts.value: REST API at https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes
facts.notes: Named-sandbox creation, session stop, async command execution and NDJSON logs are documented with HTTP bearer authentication. REST execute optionally accepts a command timeout up to 5 hours, independent of wait; this is not the session maximum or a documented default command limit.

facts.value: sandbox CLI
facts.notes: Docs describe it for manual testing and one-off commands.

facts.value: Linux images; default image includes current Node.js LTS and Python 3.14
facts.notes: Default image is vercel/sandbox/universal. Other Linux distributions can be used. SDK language does not limit the guest.

facts.value: Firecracker microVM
facts.notes: Docs say each sandbox has its own filesystem and network.

facts.value: Linux, including Ubuntu and Arch
facts.notes: Docs say Ubuntu, Arch, or any other Linux distribution you need.

facts.value: 1 vCPU, or an even number from 2 to the plan maximum. Default 2
facts.notes: Current pricing resource table, product marketing FAQ and official comparison agree: Hobby maximum 4 vCPUs, Pro 8, Enterprise 32. Repository README's Hobby/Pro 8 sentence is inconsistent with those product-specific sources; retain discrepancy as apparently stale README wording, not an unknown current Hobby cap or permission to use 8. No entitlement call made. Active CPU billing is not wall-clock time.

facts.value: Pricing says each vCPU includes 2 GB of memory. The persistence page says memory auto-scales to 2048 MB per vCPU.
facts.notes: Both units are kept and were not collapsed. Hobby maximum 8GB. Pro maximum 16GB. Enterprise maximum 64GB on the pricing page, which uses GB.

facts.value: 64 GB ephemeral NVMe; September 11 release explicitly includes deprecated runtimes
facts.notes: Current vendor-announced size is 64 GB in every Sandbox, including managed/custom images and deprecated runtime property, per September 11 release. Pricing last_updated September 10 still says legacy runtimes32 GB; preserve discrepancy as older wording superseded by explicit later expansion, not an unqualified unknown or measured allocation. No runtime call made. Drives/root snapshots independent mechanisms; GB not GiB.

facts.value: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for GPU allocation inside Vercel Sandbox
facts.notes: Broad review of current public Sandbox marketing, pricing, resource APIs and released client menus found no documented guest-GPU allocation, SKU, region or entitlement as of 2026-10-08. This is a bounded public-offering inference, not vendor denial or hardware impossibility. Remote AI Gateway and sibling Functions/build GPU are excluded. See audit E01.

facts.value: Dockerfile-built OCI images in Vercel Container Registry (VCR), plus managed/shared/public images
facts.notes: Public beta (June 30; August 12 guide still says beta). VCR images must be Ready and linux/amd64; Preparing is not usable. Private by default; share or publish for cross-project use. Current limits: compressed layers 2 GB, total layers/config 15 GB (gzip/zstd); older guide's 500 MB is stale. ENTRYPOINT/CMD do not run; set start command and WORKDIR. VCR storage: Hobby 10 GB/month included, Pro $0.10/GB-month, Enterprise custom; optimization charges beyond storage unknown. ARM64 requires API v3/v4 without runtime plus team access; general guide still says amd64, so not ungated.

facts.value: Supported
facts.notes: System packages can be built into an image. Downloaded package data is described as free network usage.

facts.value: The default Ubuntu image has full root access; execute sudo defaults to false
facts.notes: Product docs say full root access and that system-privileged processes are supported. The REST execute body has a sudo boolean, default false, described as root privileges. Both sentences are kept.

facts.value: Docker and other container engines inside the sandbox with sudo
facts.notes: Privileges are guest-only, not host privileges. Egress still follows the sandbox firewall. Containers do not inherit its proxy CA/trust variables; mount and trust the CA for HTTPS transformed or forwarded by the firewall.

facts.value: SDK detached commands and asynchronous REST command execution
facts.notes: REST returns a command ID immediately; wait true streams status. Detached services run only within the live session: stopping terminates all processes and that session cannot restart. Use onResume to restart services in a fresh session. Optional REST command timeout is 100 ms to 5 hours; not a documented default. Session lifetime is separately capped by plan.

facts.value: SDK writeFiles/readFile/downloadFile and CLI sandbox copy
facts.notes: SDK methods upload and retrieve files; CLI copy transfers one file per invocation, so archive directories before copying. Manual export is separate from filesystem snapshot recovery.

facts.value: Default persistent creation with filesystem auto-snapshot on stop/timeout, restore in a new session
facts.notes: persistent:false discards root unless snapshotted; resume boots from a usable filesystem snapshot, not live memory. Retention differs by interface: JS SDK guide 30-day last-use/1-10 or no expiry; REST v4 defaults7 days/latest; Python guide says up to100 vs REST max10. Non-resumable entities are removed after14 days. REST DELETE retains/bills snapshots by default; true removes unreferenced snapshots asynchronously. Python create/fork context managers clean up unless destroy=False; awaited calls are caller-managed and resume context only stops. Failed captures cannot restore; region/failover limits apply. Drives are separate mounted storage.

facts.value: Drives in public beta on Hobby, Pro and Enterprise
facts.notes: Mount up to 4 per run with absolute non-overlapping paths. One read-write mount per drive; many read-only point-in-time snapshot mounts after an initial write. Data persists until drive deletion; mount it in another sandbox to reuse. Drive region is immutable and must match sandbox main region; failover can read remotely with higher latency. Default size 1 TiB (1 GiB Hobby), default maximum quota 16 TiB, byte sizes multiple of 4096. Storage/read/write charges separate; deleting a drive removes data and cannot occur while attached to a running sandbox. S3/FUSE is external storage, not a Vercel Drive.

facts.value: Filesystem-based stop and automatic resume, not live process resume
facts.notes: Stopping releases allocated resources and terminates all processes. Persistent sandboxes boot a new session from the latest usable snapshot on an SDK operation; stop/update do not auto-resume. Each session receives a fresh timeout. Non-persistent sandboxes cannot resume. While stopped there is no running compute allocation, but retained snapshots/Drives keep storage billing. Waiting in a running session still bills allocated memory.

facts.value: Documented stop/resume does not preserve running processes
facts.notes: REST stop explicitly terminates all running processes and says a stopped session cannot restart. Persistent resume boots a new VM session from a filesystem snapshot; onResume restarts background services. This establishes absence of live process restoration for these documented transitions, not absence of every conceivable future memory feature.

facts.value: Filesystem/package snapshots, automatic on stop and manual snapshot()
facts.notes: Manual capture stops the session and saves filesystem/packages, not memory; uncached restore can take longer and failed captures cannot restore. Retention conflicts: JS SDK guide30-day last-use; REST v4 default7-day/latest and max10; Python guide says up to100. REST delete retains/bills snapshots unless orphan cleanup is explicitly enabled. Python create/fork contexts clean up unless destroy=False; awaited calls are caller-managed. Region availability/no migration and plan-gated failover apply. Storage: $0.08/GB-month daily-average metering, Enterprise custom; Hobby 15 GB lifetime. April latency figures are historical/cache-specific, not SLA.

facts.value: Sandbox.fork / sandbox fork from the source's current filesystem snapshot
facts.notes: Fork creates independent files from saved filesystem/config, not unsaved changes or live memory; no snapshot means a fresh source image. It is not shared Drive. Region/snapshot/failover limits apply. Current SDK fork copies source environment unless overridden; CLI --env replaces the map, not merges it. Python inherits configuration except mounts (pass mounts explicitly). Python create/fork contexts clean up unless destroy=False; awaited calls are caller-managed. REST v3 defaults7-day/latest only when omitted; current SDK uses v2. No reset/fork latency guarantee. Older clients/runtime behavior unverified.

facts.value: Available
facts.notes: Downloads from the internet are free. Data sent to the internet is billable.

facts.value: Default allow-all; deny-all including DNS; custom default-deny domain/CIDR policies with live updates
facts.notes: Full firewall is available on Hobby too. Denied CIDRs override allows. Domain rules use TLS SNI (including TLS Postgres; GSSAPI unsupported), not plaintext HTTP or HTTP Host; domain fronting may reach other virtual hosts at an allowed endpoint. Allowed CIDRs bypass domain matching/brokering/proxying; broad ranges override domain scope and CIDR-only policies leave DNS unrestricted. Transform/forwardURL rules terminate TLS, but matchers only select handling, never block: unmatched requests still pass unchanged. Catch-all * permits domain-less traffic without brokering/forwarding. To pin Host or enforce paths, apply transform/forwardURL without match and enforce policy in the proxy. No per-port policy control established. Egress controls are separate from public ingress.

facts.value: Up to 15 registered ports (1024-65535) exposed via public HTTPS URLs
facts.notes: Declare ports at creation/update; domain(port) needs a registered route. Released SDK documents full HTTPS domain, example https://subdomain.vercel.run. Web-service previews, not arbitrary raw TCP/SSH. Official app-builder starts Next.js on 0.0.0.0:3000; anyone with URL can reach it, builder password does not protect it. Not an all-protocol/all-port guarantee. Stop/snapshot ends serving session; restart on resume. Both request/response port traffic billable. Exact hostname derivation/continuity across sessions, TLS internals and general built-in preview authorization remain unknown; control-plane bearer auth does not automatically protect routes.

facts.value: Public HTTPS web previews via sandbox.domain(port), example https://subdomain.vercel.run
facts.notes: Released SDK domain() explicitly returns a full HTTPS URL; registered guest port, not caller-machine tunnel. Running session/service required, up to 15 ports, REST 1024-65535. Official app-builder binds 0.0.0.0:3000, embeds domain(3000) in iframe, URL accessible without builder password. Stable-preview marketing does not specify exact cross-session continuity; TLS internals/general auth options remain unknown. Add application protection as needed; not raw TCP/SSH ingress.

facts.value: Purchased Enterprise Secure Compute network: static egress IPs and AWS VPC peering
facts.notes: Requires an existing team network; self-service provisioning is not available to all Enterprise teams (contact account team). networkId at creation attaches immediately; updates take effect next session. Firewall still applies; deny-all removes Internet and Secure Compute access. This is connectivity to customer resources, not execution in the customer cloud or documented private sandbox-to-sandbox connectivity. Network pricing is contact-account-team; public-internet Private Data Transfer $0.15/GB, AWS peering transfer has no charge.

facts.value: Hobby 10; Pro 10,000; Enterprise 10,000 concurrent sandboxes
facts.notes: vCPU allocation rate is separate and ramps with sustained usage.

facts.value: Hobby 45 minutes; Pro 24 hours; Enterprise 24 hours
facts.notes: This is one session. Stopping and resuming resets it, so a persistent sandbox is not capped at that lifetime. Default timeout is 5 minutes unless extended.

No vendor inactivity-based Sandbox shutdown timer was documented in the reviewed lifecycle, pricing, SDK/CLI, marketing and API sources as of 2026-10-08. Keep this numeric duration unknown/null, not zero/free/unlimited; that search-based scope is not an explicit denial. The documented five-minute default is an elapsed session deadline, not idle detection; Cron cleanup and allocation reset differ. See audit E05.

facts.value: Control plane: Hobby 1,000 requests/minute; Pro 10,000; Enterprise 100,000. Deletions: 20 requests/second/team on all plans
facts.notes: Deletion also consumes control-plane quota. Dynamic vCPU allocation per minute: Hobby starts 20, ramps 20/minute to 40; Pro/Enterprise start 150, ramp 500/minute to 5,000. After 10 minutes without creation the rate returns to starting value. These are allocation-throughput quotas, not sandbox concurrency or startup latency. Enterprise increases require sales; resource and quota restrictions may limit repeated CPU rollouts even when concurrency fits.

facts.value: 19 regions, default iad1
facts.notes: Codes on the regions page: arn1, bom1, cdg1, cle1, cpt1, dub1, fra1, gru1, hkg1, hnd1, iad1, icn1, kix1, lhr1, pdx1, sfo1, sin1, syd1, and yul1. Failover regions are unavailable on Hobby and Pro trial. Active CPU, memory, data transfer, and drive rates vary by region. Creation and snapshot storage rates do not.

facts.value: NDJSON command logs
facts.notes: GET /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/cmd/{cmdId}/logs streams stdout, stderr, and error. Execute can also set logs true when wait is true.

facts.value: Logs are listed as available from a sandbox
facts.notes: Product page mentions access to logs, file edits, and live previews.

facts.value: sandbox connect interactive shell; exec/run --interactive --tty with terminal sizing/resizing
facts.notes: Published CLI 4.6.1 uses SDK openInteractive() to obtain WebSocket URL/token; start frame includes terminal columns/rows and SIGWINCH sends resize frames. This resolves terminal size/resize mechanism, not a raw public SSH listener or preview-auth contract. CLI periodically extends session unless --no-extend-timeout; not idle detection. Python SDK explicitly lacks interactive PTY shells; its console commands delegate to JS CLI through npx and require Node.js. No paid runtime test.

facts.value: Firewall credential brokering injects HTTP headers on egress; credentials stay outside the guest
facts.notes: Available on Hobby too. HTTP handling on allowed domains; unmatched requests lack credentials. TLS/SNI needed, catch-all/CIDR bypasses and Postgres transforms ignored. HTTP interception uses a per-sandbox CA at /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/sandbox-proxy-ca.crt. Default guest runtimes preconfigure trust, but nested Docker containers, independent trust stores or certificate-pinned clients must also trust that CA or HTTPS brokering can fail; Node clients can use NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. Brokered credentials distinct from guest-visible sandbox/command env. No general guest vault/rotation/per-secret IAM established. Current CLI 4.6.1/SDK 3.5.1 server-side fork inherits source env unless overridden; CLI --env replaces whole map. CLI reference says not copied, but released code and REST server-copy contract establish current inheritance, so treat guest env secrets as propagated, not automatically removed. No paid runtime test.

facts.value: Control-plane project OIDC or scoped access token; private-beta Sandboxes read/read-write project permissions
facts.notes: Local OIDC expires12h, Vercelproduction manages expiry. External SDK callers use team/project IDs and authorized access token. Sign in with Vercel permission table explicitly offers project Sandboxes Read Only or Read and Write, but API/team-resource permission grants are private beta; do not imply general availability or a per-action/per-secret matrix. General team RBAC Pro/Enterprise and contributor project roles Enterprise are documented, without Sandbox action mapping in retrieved role references. These authenticate management, not automatically public preview URLs; built-in preview authorization remains unknown.

facts.value: Coding agents in the default image, plus an ecosystem page
facts.notes: The default image includes coding agents. Named integrations were not copied from the ecosystem page.

facts.value: Apache-2.0 for the vercel/sandbox SDK/CLI repository
facts.notes: LICENSE read directly on 2026-10-08; repository also publishes managed image sources. This does not establish an open-source hosted Sandbox server or self-hostable control plane.

network_isolation.note: Separate network namespace plus firewall: default allow-all, deny-all including DNS, custom default-deny. Egress policy does not disable separately exposed public ingress; SNI/domain-fronting and CIDR/DNS bypass qualifications apply.

egress_allowlist.note: Custom default-deny domain/CIDR allowlists on all plans; deny CIDRs override. SNI is not HTTP Host enforcement; CIDR allows bypass domains/brokering and can leave DNS unrestricted. Matchers never block; catch-all permits unhandled domain-less traffic.

inbound_ports_or_preview_urls.note: Up to 15 ports (REST 1024-65535), public web URLs via domain(port) and HTTPS route examples; running service/session required. Official Next.js example binds 0.0.0.0:3000, URL accessible to anyone with it. Not raw TCP/SSH or a general preview-auth/URL continuity guarantee.

private_networking.note: Purchased Enterprise Secure Compute network required; not all teams can provision self-service. Static egress and AWS VPC peering, not BYOC. networkId changes require next session. Contact-account-team network fee and Private Data Transfer apply.

snapshots.note: Filesystem/manual-stop. JSguide30day TTL vs RESTv4 default7day/latest; RESTcountmax10 vs Pyguide100. RESTdelete retains bydefault/optionalorphan cleanup. Python create/fork asynccontexts clean unless destroy=False; resumecontext onlystops. Regions/storage/daily-average metering apply; failed capture cannot restore.

memory_snapshot_or_live_resume.note: Documented stop terminates all running processes; stopped sessions cannot restart. Resume creates a fresh VM from filesystem state and onResume restarts services, not live memory/process restoration.

pause_resume.note: Filesystem-based stop/resume resets session duration; releases compute and terminates processes. Non-persistent sandboxes cannot resume; usable retained snapshot required. Storage still bills while stopped; waiting in a live session bills memory.

cloning_forking.note: Latest saved filesystem/config, not unsaved live state; no snapshot fresh image. Current CLI 4.6.1/SDK 3.5.1 call server fork API, which copies env; --env replaces whole map. Released source resolves inheritance despite stale CLI exclusion wording. Region/retention restrictions remain; not memory clone.

persistent_filesystem.note: Default persistent create/file-based restore, not memory; JSguide30day TTL vs RESTv4 default7day/latest. RESTdelete retains unless optionalorphancleanup. Python create/fork asynccontexts destroy/clean unless destroy=False, resumecontext onlystops. Expiry/failure can lose restore; sudden-failure guarantee unknown, storage separate.

volumes.note: Drives public beta on all plans; up to 4 mounts, one writer per drive and many initialized read-only snapshots. Region match required except failover. Persists until drive deletion, must remount to reuse; logical storage/read/write charges are separate from root snapshots.

custom_images.note: Custom images publicly beta per release/current VCR guide; prepared Ready linux/amd64 in project-scoped VCR. Sharing needed cross-project; no ENTRYPOINT/CMD. Current limits 2 GB/layer,15 GB total; older guide500 MB differs. Pro VCR $0.10/GB-month, Hobby10 GB/month included, Enterprise custom. ARM64 gated, not general support.

docker_in_sandbox.note: Docker engines supported with guest sudo; firewall remains applicable. Containers need their own proxy CA trust for transformed/forwarded HTTPS; no host privilege implied.

root_sudo.note: The default Ubuntu image is described as having full root access, and the execute API sudo flag defaults to false.

gpu.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for guest GPU allocation after Q01/Q06/Q07/Q09/Q21/Q22 and full marketing/pricing/runtime/API/client review. False is conservative comparison eligibility, not a vendor denial or impossible-hardware claim. Remote inference is not guest GPU; scope/URLs/access log in audit E01.

self_hosted.note: Official Sandbox vs E2B comparison updated 2026-09-04 explicitly says Vercel Sandbox does not currently offer self-hosting; open SDK/CLI/images are not a self-hostable service. Product-specific negative, not missing-doc inference.

byoc.note: Sandbox-specific comparison says no BYOC, but newer company platform/pricing markets Enterprise AWS BYOC without establishing Sandbox inclusion/control-plane/access model. Product-scope uncertainty retained; Secure Compute peering is not BYOC; linked docs/byoc404.

open_source.note: The vercel/sandbox repository license is Apache-2.0; that file is not the hosted sandbox service.

background_processes.note: Detached SDK/asynchronous REST commands run in a live session. Stop terminates all processes; restart services onResume. Optional REST command timeout up to 5 hours is separate from session limits.

terminal_pty.note: Published CLI 4.6.1 starts authenticated WebSocket interactive shell with cols/rows and SIGWINCH resize frames. --tty terminal features, optional timeout extension not idle detection. Python API lacks PTY; its console command delegates to Node.js CLI. Not raw public SSH ingress.

command_streaming.note: The REST reference includes GET .../cmd/{cmdId}/logs to stream command logs.

secrets_management.note: HTTP egress broker outside guest, not generic vault: SNI/handling/CIDR/catch-all/Postgres restrictions. HTTPS interception requires trust in /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/sandbox-proxy-ca.crt; default guest trust is configured, but nested Docker, independent trust stores or certificate-pinned clients need compatible CA trust (for Node, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS). Env is guest-visible; current published CLI/SDK server fork inherits env unless overridden, despite stale CLI reference. --env replaces map. Treat env secrets as copied, not automatically stripped.

python_sdk.note: The sandbox nav lists a Python SDK that uses vercel.sandbox from the vercel package.

typescript_sdk.note: The sandbox nav lists a JavaScript SDK at @vercel/sandbox.

go_sdk.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for an official Go Sandbox client SDK after Q15/Q28, product docs, ecosystem, general TypeScript REST SDK and official repo inspection. False is documented-support audit eligibility, not vendor denial; JS/TS/Python, HTTP clients and guest Go execution are distinct. Scope/access log in audit E02.

cli.note: The sandbox nav lists a sandbox CLI for manual testing and one-off commands.

mcp_or_agent_integrations.note: The default image includes coding agents, and the sandbox nav has an Ecosystem section for agent frameworks.

max_vcpu.note: Pricing, product FAQ and comparison agree Enterprise32/Pro8/Hobby4. README Hobby/Pro8 appears stale; discrepancy preserved without treating current Hobby4 cap as unknown. No live entitlement test.

max_memory_gib.note: Pricing maximum is Enterprise 64GB, Pro 16GB, Hobby 8GB; SDK/persistence say 2048 MB per vCPU. Sources do not establish a GiB maximum; no GB-to-GiB normalization is made.

max_session_duration_seconds.note: Pro and Enterprise maximum session duration is 24 hours; Hobby is 45 minutes, and stopping and resuming resets the session.

idle_timeout_seconds.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for inactivity-based shutdown after Q12. Numeric duration remains unknown/null, not false/zero/unlimited. No idle feature eligibility inferred. Default5-minute creation timeout is a session deadline, not idle detection; audit inference distinct from vendor denial (E05).

pricing_summary: Published USD Sandbox rates in iad1: $0.128/Active CPU hour, $0.0212/GB-hour allocated memory (including wait/idle, 1-minute minimum), $0.60/1M creations, $0.08/GB-month snapshots and Drive storage/reads/writes $0.05/GB-month, $0.0015/GB, $0.004/GB. Regional rates vary except creation/snapshots. Pro requires $20/month platform fee with one deploying seat and shared $20/month usage credit. Transfer included only in enabled/eligible Flat Rate CDN with capacity tiers; Enterprise pricing/quotas are negotiated/custom, not guaranteed table rates. Personal non-commercial Hobby hard quotas, no overage; reset wording conflicts. Default persistence creates billable snapshots unless opted out. Marketing pricing resolves beta VCR storage: Pro $0.10/GB-month, Hobby 10 GB/month included, Enterprise custom; reference omits period. Enterprise Secure Compute purchased/contact-price plus $0.15/GB Internet Private Data Transfer, peering uncharged. No computed workload bill/latency benchmark inferred.

pricing.conditions: Non-commercial personal Hobby use only, no overage charge. Active CPU excludes I/O wait, not allocated memory costs. Creation pauses at quota: one paragraph says until next billing cycle, another says 30 days since first use; Hobby plan page says no billing cycles. Reset wording unresolved.

pricing.published_price: Table rate $0.128/Active CPU hour in iad1
pricing.conditions: Marketing pricing explicitly says Enterprise Custom, corroborating docs custom terms: the Enterprise table number is a published reference, not a guaranteed negotiated contract. Pro rate at iad1, other regions differ. Active CPU excludes I/O waiting. Official comparison describes millisecond Active CPU granularity but does not establish minimum rounding increment; memory separately has 1-minute minimum, so do not apply millisecond billing to all meters. No counterfactual workload bill or 95% savings assumed.
Non-commercial personal Hobby only, hard quota/no paid overage. Allocated memory includes idle/I/O waiting with 1-minute minimum increments. GB is not GiB.

iad1 table rate; regional rates vary and Enterprise terms are custom. Pricing says 2 GB per vCPU; SDK/persistence say 2048 MB per vCPU, not collapsed into GiB. Allocated memory bills while running, including idle/I/O wait, in 1-minute minimum increments. No running compute allocation after stop; retained storage charges remain.
Each Sandbox.create() counts as one. Non-commercial personal Hobby only, hard quota; no paid overage. Creation throughput and concurrency quotas also apply.
Table rate same in every Sandbox region; each Sandbox.create counts regardless of duration. Enterprise pricing/quotas custom. No numeric separate fork/resume/snapshot operation charge established.

Non-commercial personal Hobby only, hard quota/no paid overage. Internet downloads free; sends plus both request and response traffic through exposed ports count. Do not interpret all ingress as free.

Sandbox pricing table; not unconditional unlimited transfer. Flat Rate CDN must be enabled and workload eligible. Lowest capacity tier included with Pro: 1M requests and 1 TB/month, shared across covered resources. Higher $20/$100/$300 monthly tiers and capacity limits apply; out-of-scope bulk/file/media distribution may be excluded. Disabled Flat Rate CDN moves to on-demand rates; no standalone Pro Sandbox on-demand transfer rate established here. Downloads from the Internet are free, but both directions of exposed-port traffic are billable.

Non-commercial personal Hobby only. Lifetime allowance not a monthly GB-month rate. Default persistence produces snapshots automatically; opt out with persistent:false. Snapshot expiry/deletion controls retained storage.

iad1 table rate, regional rates vary; Enterprise terms custom. Drives public beta. Billed logical used size measured hourly, not provisioned size; persists and bills until drive deletion. Hobby 15 GB lifetime is a different allowance, not paid storage rate.

iad1 table rate, regional rates vary; Enterprise custom terms. Public-beta Drive logical read usage, separate from compute/storage. Hobby includes 30 GB/month under non-commercial personal-use quotas.

iad1 table rate, regional rates vary; Enterprise custom terms. Public-beta Drive logical write usage, separate from compute/storage. Hobby includes 30 GB/month under non-commercial personal-use quotas.

pricing.published_price: $20/month recurring usage credit included in the paid Pro platform fee
pricing.conditions: Shared across managed infrastructure, not $20 dedicated to Sandbox or promotional signup credit. Expires/reset monthly; on-demand usage after exhaustion. The $20/month platform fee remains payable; additional deploying seats $20/month each.

One deploying seat and $20/month shared infrastructure usage credit included. USD excludes applicable taxes. This is the required Pro subscription, not a separate Sandbox-only fee; do not count credit as an independent free plan.

Sandbox sends to Internet plus both directions of exposed-port traffic; Internet downloads free. Regional transfer rates vary. Enterprise section separately says custom pricing/quotas and contact sales: table is not a guaranteed negotiated rate.

Same reference rate across Sandbox regions, Enterprise negotiated terms custom. August 31 release: each day's average usage added to monthly invoice, effective next billing period, not a whole-month retention minimum. Default persistence snapshots on stop/timeout; persistent:false opts out. REST delete retains snapshots by default; optional deleteOrphanSnapshots:true asynchronously removes unreferenced ones. TTL version matters: current persistence guide 30-day last-use expiry versus REST v4 7-day default/only-latest retention; configure explicitly. Python retention count 1-100 conflicts with REST v3/v4 max10; do not promise100. No separate snapshot creation/restore or root-disk rate established; missing price is not free.

pricing.published_price: Free within quotas; 15 GB snapshot storage lifetime, 15 GB Drive storage lifetime, 30 GB/month Drive reads, 30 GB/month Drive writes
pricing.conditions: Non-commercial personal use only. Lifetime storage allowance wording is distinct from monthly compute/I/O allowances and is not normalized into GB-months. No overage charge; creation pauses. Pricing conflicts on next billing cycle versus 30 days since first use; Hobby plan page says there are no billing cycles. Drives public beta.

Official marketing pricing explicitly supplies the missing period for Vercel Container Registry Image Storage (Beta), used by Functions and Sandbox; VCR reference/guide shorten to $0.10 per GB (guide says across all plans), so preserve their less-specific wording rather than silently infer it. No dedicated Pro allowance specified in VCR row; do not assume free storage beyond shared platform credit. CLI build local Docker/Podman/Buildah; VCR prepares optimized snapshots in background without user spinning up a Sandbox. Separate optimization/build charges not established, not assumed free.

pricing.published_price: Network: contact account team; Private Data Transfer $0.15/GB
pricing.conditions: Sandbox attachment needs an existing Enterprise Secure Compute network. Public-internet traffic leaving the private network bills Private Data Transfer; traffic over AWS VPC peering has no transfer charge. Do not treat this as free BYOC or assume how it stacks with ordinary Sandbox transfer without confirmation.
